cells.tense: The mind is at home in its own depths, with the pen still moving.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Set the question you're carrying in this half-lit stretch down for one hour. No task on the hour, no answer owed. Be with what your heart holds about it, and stop there.
cells.core:
You can go deep into a question with no clear shape and not need the whole road visible. Enough light for the next step is enough. The pattern surfaces when it surfaces, and you don't force the answer before it's ready. That is the work going well.

This balance is free to feed the feeling under the thinking. Set the question down for one hour, with no task attached to the hour, and stay with what your heart holds about it. Not another angle, not a better frame — just that. What the heart keeps and what the mind finds turn out to be the same finding here, and one can rest the other. What you hold doesn't need defending.

cells.tense: The mind is pushing for the whole shape before the fog has cleared.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: When the uncertainty is thick and others are in it with you, say how you see it laid out — once, plainly. Don't argue for it. Put that out there and go quiet.
cells.core:
You can go deep into a question that has no clear shape — that part is real. But the depth is reaching past what this moment has given you. The pattern gets asserted before it's been found. The next step gets forced because the whole road isn't visible yet, and the people standing beside you in the fog get the finished shape before the terrain.

What settles it is offering the shape instead of imposing it. Say how you see it laid out, once, to whoever is in this with you. Plainly, without arguing for it. A frame spoken before anyone asks gives people something to stand in — you included. The depth stops reaching when the shape has somewhere to land.

cells.tense: The mind is standing at a door it already walked through, still waiting for it to open.
cells.act: share the joy with the people it belongs to
cells.ask: Tell someone the good thing that's actually happening in this half-lit stretch — out loud, before it's finished, before you've decided it counts. Share it as it is, not as a report on it.
cells.core:
Moving through uncertainty without forcing clarity is what this does when it runs. Here it isn't running. The fog gets treated as a reason to wait — for the whole road, for the pattern to resolve, for something to be finished enough to act on. The depth is still in you. It's just not coming out to play.

What pulls you back is sharing a good thing that's actually happening, out loud, before it's finished, before you've decided it counts. Say it to one of the people it belongs to. You don't need the whole road to say what's good. Gladness travels outward when it's spoken, and the speaking puts you back where you already stand.

cells.tense: The mind is deep in the pattern while the story you tell is that you're just watching.
cells.act: rest in the connection without doing anything with it
cells.ask: When the fog is shared with someone, stay in it and do nothing with it. No frame, no next step, no resolution. Just be there beside them inside it.
cells.core:
You go deep into a question that has no clear shape, and the account you give leaves the depth unclaimed — it was just what the situation required, just following the thread where it led. But the thread was followed. The pattern was seen. The next step was found in the fog. That's the work, and whoever did it has quietly slid past the credit.

Simpler than the depth itself is what returns it: rest in the connection without doing anything with it. When the fog is shared with someone, don't resolve it, don't frame it, don't find the next step. Be in it with them, and treat that as the whole of what you do. What you understand about it is already there. Sitting with someone inside it is the form you can keep.
